name: Ezer
overview: Ezer was a male member of the tribe of Ephraim, known particularly as the grandson of Ephraim. His life is marked by a tragic end, as he was killed by the men of Gath. This brief but significant detail situates him within the ongoing conflicts faced by Israel in the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezer is a proper name meaning 'help.' It was not given by God but reflects a common Hebrew name with a straightforward meaning related to assistance or support.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Ezer was the grandson of Ephraim, linking him directly to this prominent tribal ancestor. No further family relationships beyond this are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ezer's significance lies in his identification as a descendant of Ephraim, connecting him to one of Israel's leading tribes. His death at the hands of the men of Gath highlights the ongoing struggles and hostilities Israel faced from surrounding peoples. Though his mention is brief, it contributes to the historical and genealogical record important for understanding the tribal dynamics and conflicts in Israel's history.
